title: Psalms and Proverbs
subtitle: Wisdom and prayer for daily life

guide.summary: The Psalms of trust teach us that no matter the difficulties, we can always trust in God's care. He is our protector, refuge and strength in moments of fear.

keyVerses.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?
He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High shall lodge under the shadow of the Almighty.

exercises.text: "The LORD is my shepherd, I shall not _____."
exercises.speaker: David
exercises.explanation: When God is our shepherd, He provides all our needs, whether food, protection, or love.

exercises.statement: Psalm 23 compares God to a shepherd who cares for his sheep.
exercises.explanation: David uses the image of the shepherd to express God's loving care and protection.

exercises.prompt: What does 'the valley of the shadow of death' mean in Psalm 23?
exercises.text: "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil."
options: The moments of greatest difficulty and fear
exercises.answer: The moments of greatest difficulty and fear
exercises.explanation: Even in adversity, we trust that God is with us and protects us.

exercises.text: God's promise in Psalm 23:4
tokens: through the valley of the shadow of death

exercises.text: The LORD is my light and my salvation.
options: The LORD is my protector and defender
The LORD is my light and salvation
The LORD is my judge and king
exercises.answer: The LORD is my light and salvation

exercises.text: "The LORD is my light and my _____."

exercises.statement: Trusting in God means we will never face difficulties.
exercises.explanation: Trusting in God does not mean being free from difficulties, but knowing that He is with us in every situation.

exercises.text: "God is our refuge and fortress, a very present help in _____."
exercises.speaker: Psalmist
exercises.explanation: In all trouble, we can run to God's refuge and find security.

exercises.statement: Psalm 46 speaks about God defeating enemies in a literal battle.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 46 is mainly about God as spiritual refuge, with poetic language about divine trust.

exercises.prompt: What is the central message of Psalm 46:10?
exercises.text: "Be still, and know that I am God."
options: Rest in God and acknowledge His authority
exercises.answer: Rest in God and acknowledge His authority
exercises.explanation: Stillness allows us to trust and accept God's supreme dominion in our lives.

exercises.text: God's promise in Psalm 46:1
God is our refuge and fortress.
"Be still, and know that I am _____."

exercises.statement: God promises that if we trust in Him, we will not face wars or conflicts.
exercises.explanation: God promises to be with us and be our strength in difficulties, not necessarily to spare us from them.

exercises.text: "He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High shall lodge under the shadow of the _____."
exercises.speaker: Psalmist
exercises.explanation: Whoever trusts in the all-powerful God finds refuge and rest in His protection.

exercises.statement: Psalm 91 promises that God protects us from all danger with His wings.
exercises.explanation: The image of God's wings symbolizes protection, safety, and maternal care.

exercises.prompt: What does Psalm 91:2 say about God?
exercises.text: "I will say of the LORD, 'He is my refuge and my _____."
exercises.explanation: God is our refuge (protection) and our fortress (stronghold), a safe place.

exercises.text: God's protection in Psalm 91:4
He will cover you with his feathers.
options: God will give you wings to fly
God will cover you with his feathers
exercises.answer: God will cover you with his feathers

exercises.text: "You are my refuge and my _____."

exercises.statement: God's protection in Psalm 91 includes protection from all kinds of evil.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 91 speaks about spiritual protection and trust, not exemption from all physical suffering.

exercises.prompt: Who is the 'Most High' in Psalm 91?
exercises.text: "He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High..."
exercises.explanation: Most High is one of God's names that expresses His supremacy and absolute power.

exercises.statement: Psalm 91 was written by David when he was fleeing from Saul.
exercises.explanation: The author of Psalm 91 is not identified; it is a psalm of trust for anyone in difficult times.

exercises.prompt: What is the condition for receiving protection in Psalm 91:9-10?
exercises.text: "Because you have said, 'The LORD is my refuge.'"
exercises.explanation: God's protection is available to those who choose Him as refuge and trust in Him.

exercises.text: Trust in God in Psalm 91:2
tokens: I will say to the LORD

exercises.text: Because you have said The LORD is my refuge.
"He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High, under the shadow of the Almighty _____."

exercises.statement: God's protection in Psalm 91 is only for the perfectly righteous.
exercises.explanation: God's protection is available to all those who seek refuge in Him with genuine faith.

exercises.prompt: Which psalm begins with 'The LORD is my shepherd'?
exercises.text: This is one of the most famous psalms about trust in God.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 23 is the most well-known psalm of trust, using the image of shepherd and sheep.

exercises.statement: All the psalms of trust were written by David.
exercises.explanation: Many psalms were written by David, but others were written by different authors throughout Israel's history.

exercises.prompt: What image does God use to protect in Psalm 91?
exercises.text: This comparison expresses maternal care and total protection.
exercises.explanation: The image of wings symbolizes God's embracing protection for His children.

exercises.text: Verse of trust summarized
The LORD is my shepherd, I shall not want.

exercises.prompt: Match the psalm to the theme
Put in order the characteristics of trust
exercises.text: Progress of trust in God

exercises.statement: Trust in God protects us from all and any suffering.
exercises.explanation: Trust in God gives us spiritual security and His presence, not elimination of all difficulties.

guide.summary: The Psalms of praise and gratitude teach us to celebrate God's wonderful works and to be grateful for the blessings received. Gratitude transforms us and brings us closer to God.

keyVerses.text: Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth!
Bless the LORD, my soul; and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
Praise him with tambourine and dance.

exercises.text: "Make a joyful noise to God, all the _____."
exercises.speaker: Psalmist
exercises.explanation: Praise to God should be universal and involve all of creation in genuine joy.

exercises.statement: Psalm 100 is a psalm of praise that exhorts people to praise God with joy.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 100 is entirely dedicated to joyful praise and gratitude to God.

exercises.prompt: Why should we praise God according to Psalm 100:5?
exercises.text: "For the LORD is good; his mercy is _____."
exercises.explanation: God's goodness and mercy are constant and never end, reason enough for praise.

exercises.text: Call to praise in Psalm 100:1-2
Serve the LORD with gladness!
options: Sing to the LORD with power

exercises.text: "For the LORD is good; his mercy is _____."

exercises.statement: Praising God with gladness is only for the good times of life.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 100 calls us to praise with joy regardless of circumstances, as an act of faith.

exercises.text: "Bless the LORD, my soul; and all that is within me bless his _____."
exercises.speaker: David
exercises.explanation: All of our essence should praise and bless God's holy name.

exercises.statement: Psalm 103 is an individual psalm that expresses gratitude for God's works.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 103 is a powerful psalm of thanksgiving for God's blessings and mercies.

exercises.prompt: According to Psalm 103, what is God's attitude toward us?
exercises.text: "The LORD is merciful and _____, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love."
exercises.explanation: God's graciousness means His willingness to forgive and treat us with compassion.

exercises.text: Call to gratitude in Psalm 103:1-2
Bless the LORD my soul.
"The LORD is merciful and _____, slow to anger."

exercises.statement: God wants us to forget none of His benefits.
exercises.explanation: God wants us to remember ALL of His benefits to keep our gratitude and praise alive.

exercises.text: "Praise the LORD! For it is good to sing ___ to our God."
exercises.speaker: Psalmist
exercises.explanation: Singing hymns of praise is a powerful way to express our worship to God.

exercises.statement: Psalm 119 is the longest psalm of the Bible and deals with God's Law.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 119 has 176 verses divided into 22 stanzas, each beginning with a letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

exercises.prompt: What is the main theme of Psalm 119?
exercises.text: This psalm speaks about the importance of meditating on God's Law.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 119 celebrates God's Law and Word as a source of wisdom, direction, and life.

exercises.text: Praise for God's Word in Psalm 119:105
Your word is a lamp to my feet.
options: Your word is a lamp to my feet
exercises.answer: Your word is a lamp to my feet

exercises.text: "_____ is a lamp to my feet."

exercises.statement: God's Word illuminates and guides us on the right path.
exercises.explanation: God's Word functions as a lamp that illuminates and guides our steps in life.

exercises.text: "Praise the LORD, all peoples; praise him, all _____."
exercises.speaker: Psalmist
exercises.explanation: Praise to God is universal and should be shared by all peoples of the earth.

exercises.statement: Psalm 117 is the shortest psalm of the Bible with only two verses.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 117 is indeed the shortest of the 150 psalms, containing only two verses of universal praise.

exercises.prompt: According to Psalm 136, what is the reason for each praise?
exercises.text: Each verse ends with the same declaration.
options: Because He is worthy of praise
exercises.explanation: Psalm 136 repeats this statement 26 times, emphasizing the constancy of God's mercy.

exercises.text: Universal praise in Psalm 117
tokens: and the truth of the LORD

exercises.text: His mercy endures forever.
"Because His mercy endures _____."

exercises.statement: Praise to God is relevant only at certain special moments.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 136 emphasizes that we should praise God continuously because His mercy endures forever.

exercises.prompt: What is the central theme of the psalms of praise?
exercises.text: These psalms encourage us to express joy and gratitude.
exercises.explanation: The psalms of praise focus on celebrating who God is and what He has done for us.

exercises.statement: Gratitude protects us from falling into depression and despair.
exercises.explanation: Recognizing God's blessings and expressing gratitude keeps us focused on His goodness.

exercises.prompt: How should we praise according to Psalm 150?
exercises.text: This psalm describes instruments and forms of praise.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 150 invites expressive and joyful praise through various means.

exercises.text: Summary of the call to praise
Make a joyful noise to God all the earth.
options: Make a joyful noise to God
exercises.answer: Make a joyful noise to God

exercises.prompt: Match the psalm to the praise theme

exercises.text: Progression of genuine praise

exercises.statement: Praise to God should be a continuous part of our life, not just occasional.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 136 emphasizes continuous praise because God's mercy is constant.

guide.summary: Proverbs teach us practical wisdom for living well. They speak of genuine friendship, honest work, words that heal, and humility. Wisdom fears the LORD and guides us in all decisions.

keyVerses.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.
A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
Train up a child in the way he should go.

exercises.text: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of _____."
exercises.speaker: Wisdom
exercises.explanation: True wisdom begins with respect and reverence for God.

exercises.statement: Wisdom comes mainly from learning with others.
exercises.explanation: Although we learn from others, true wisdom is rooted in the fear of the LORD.

exercises.prompt: What does 'fear of the LORD' mean?
exercises.text: This concept does not mean to be afraid as if fleeing, but something different.
exercises.explanation: The fear of the LORD is reverence with love, acknowledging His authority and goodness.

exercises.text: The foundation of wisdom
tokens: and knowledge of the Holy One

exercises.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.
options: The fear of the LORD is beginning of wisdom
exercises.answer: The fear of the LORD is beginning of wisdom

exercises.text: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of _____."

exercises.statement: A wise person recognizes that he does not know everything and continues learning.
exercises.explanation: True wisdom includes humility and a continuous willingness to learn more.

exercises.text: "Gracious words are like a honeycomb, sweetness to the soul and health to the _____."
exercises.speaker: Wisdom
exercises.explanation: Our words have the power to heal or hurt, to build or destroy.

exercises.statement: Cruel words hurt, but afterward we forget them.
exercises.explanation: Hurtful words cut deeply and leave lasting emotional scars.

exercises.prompt: What is the value of a gentle answer?
exercises.text: "A soft answer turns away _____, but a harsh word stirs up anger."
exercises.explanation: Soft and gentle words can calm even tense situations.

exercises.text: The power of words in Proverbs 18:21
A soft answer turns away wrath.
options: A soft answer turns away wrath
exercises.answer: A soft answer turns away wrath

exercises.prompt: Match types of words to their effect

exercises.text: "Death and life are in the power of the _____."

exercises.statement: We should think about our words before speaking.
exercises.explanation: Our words have consequences, so it is wise to think before speaking.

exercises.text: "A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for _____."
exercises.speaker: Wisdom
exercises.explanation: A true friend is always by our side, especially in difficult times.

exercises.statement: A true friendship is one that remains only in times of joy.
exercises.explanation: True friendship shows itself especially in moments of difficulty and suffering.

exercises.text: "Walk with the wise and become wise, but the companion of _____ will suffer."
exercises.explanation: Friendships influence our lives, so we should choose companions who help us grow.

exercises.text: The value of companionship in Proverbs 13:20
A friend loves at all times.
options: A friend loves at all times
exercises.answer: A friend loves at all times

exercises.text: "A friend loves at all _____, and a brother is born for adversity."

exercises.statement: Our friendships do not have a significant impact on who we become.
exercises.explanation: Our friendships profoundly influence our character and life decisions.

exercises.text: "The sluggard craves and gets nothing, but the desires of the diligent are fully _____."
exercises.speaker: Wisdom
exercises.explanation: Diligent and persevering work leads to achievement and success.

exercises.statement: Laziness is seen as a natural weakness in Proverbs.
exercises.explanation: Laziness in Proverbs is portrayed as a choice that leads to poverty and failure.

exercises.prompt: What does Proverbs say about humility?
exercises.text: "Humility comes before _____."
exercises.explanation: Humility precedes any true honor; it is the basis of respectable character.

exercises.text: Promise about diligent work
The diligent hand will come to power but laziness leads to forced labor.
"The sluggard craves and gets nothing, but the desires of the diligent are fully _____."

exercises.statement: Humility and hard work are lasting principles in Proverbs.
exercises.explanation: Humility and diligence are fundamental values that lead to a successful and honored life.

exercises.prompt: What is the central theme of Proverbs?
exercises.text: This book was written mainly to teach how to live well.
exercises.explanation: Proverbs offers practical advice on how to make good decisions in life.

exercises.statement: Fear of the LORD is important only in religious context.
exercises.explanation: Fear of the LORD is the foundation for all practical wisdom and wise decisions in life.

exercises.prompt: How should we care with our words?
exercises.text: Proverbs emphasizes the power and responsibility of speech.
options: Care that they are true and kind
Say what others want to hear
exercises.answer: Care that they are true and kind
exercises.explanation: Our words have power to heal or hurt, so we should be careful and respectful.

exercises.text: Summary of practical wisdom
Walk with the wise and become wise.
options: Walk with the wise become wise
exercises.answer: Walk with the wise become wise

exercises.text: Progress in acquiring wisdom

exercises.statement: Wisdom is a gift that comes mainly from our experiences.
exercises.explanation: Although we learn from experience, true wisdom originates in the fear of the LORD.

guide.summary: Prayer is genuine conversation with God. Repentance is a change of heart that transforms us. Through these, we experience forgiveness, renewal, and intimacy with our Creator.

keyVerses.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
O LORD, you have searched me and known me.
Pray therefore like this: Our Father in heaven...

exercises.text: "Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right _____ within me."
exercises.speaker: David
exercises.explanation: True repentance leads to the desire for a renewed heart and upright spirit.

exercises.statement: Psalm 51 is the most well-known repentance psalm, written by David after his sin.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 51 is a powerful psalm of confession and repentance after David's sin.

exercises.text: "Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my _____."
exercises.explanation: God washes and cleanses us when we sincerely repent of our sins.

exercises.text: Prayer of repentance in Psalm 51:1-2
tokens: Have mercy on me, O God

exercises.text: Create in me a clean heart O God.
options: Create in me a clean heart
exercises.answer: Create in me a clean heart

exercises.text: "Create in me a _____ heart, O God, and renew a right spirit."

exercises.statement: Repentance is merely feeling remorse for sins.
exercises.explanation: True repentance includes confession, genuine remorse, and change of life.

exercises.text: "O LORD, you have searched me and _____."
exercises.speaker: David
exercises.explanation: God knows deeply every aspect of our life and heart.

exercises.statement: Psalm 139 expresses that God is always present and knows us completely.
exercises.explanation: Psalm 139 is a profound psalm about God's omniscience and omnipresence.

exercises.prompt: What is the comfort in Psalm 139:5?
exercises.text: "You hem me in, _____, and behind, and lay your hand upon me."
exercises.explanation: God surrounds us completely and His presence protects us in all directions.

exercises.text: God's presence in Psalm 139:7-8
O LORD you search me and know me.
options: O LORD you search and know me
exercises.answer: O LORD you search and know me

exercises.text: "O LORD, you have searched me and _____."

exercises.statement: We can hide our thoughts from God.
exercises.explanation: God knows not only our actions but also our most secret thoughts.

exercises.text: "Our Father, who art in _____."
exercises.speaker: Jesus
exercises.explanation: The prayer begins by recognizing God as our Father in heaven.

exercises.statement: The Lord's Prayer was taught by Jesus as a model for prayer.
exercises.explanation: Jesus taught us this prayer as an example of how we should pray to the Father.

exercises.prompt: What is the second petition of the Lord's Prayer?
exercises.text: "Your kingdom come, your _____ be done, on earth as it is in heaven."
exercises.explanation: We ask that God's will be done in our lives and in the world.

exercises.text: Petition for bread in Matthew 6:11
Your kingdom come your will be done.
options: Your kingdom come your will done
exercises.answer: Your kingdom come your will done

exercises.prompt: Match the petitions of the Lord's Prayer

exercises.text: "Our daily bread give us _____."

exercises.statement: The Lord's Prayer contains petitions only for ourselves.
exercises.explanation: The Lord's Prayer includes petitions to glorify God, for His kingdom to come, and for forgiveness.

exercises.text: "Vanity of vanities, says the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is _____."
exercises.speaker: Ecclesiastes
exercises.explanation: Ecclesiastes makes us reflect that life without God is empty and without lasting meaning.

exercises.statement: Ecclesiastes teaches that everything we do without God is empty and purposeless.
exercises.explanation: Ecclesiastes shows that without God, all our search for meaning is futile.

exercises.prompt: What is the conclusion of Ecclesiastes?
exercises.text: "Now all has been heard; here is the conclusion of the matter: Fear God and _____ his commandments."
exercises.explanation: After exploring everything in life, the conclusion is that we should fear God and keep His commandments.

exercises.text: The central message in Ecclesiastes 3:1
There is a time for everything under heaven.
options: There is a time for everything heaven
exercises.answer: There is a time for everything heaven

exercises.text: "There is a time for every purpose under _____."

exercises.statement: Life has meaning when we place God at the center of everything.
exercises.explanation: When we fear God and keep His commandments, our life gains eternal purpose.

exercises.prompt: What is the purpose of repentance?
exercises.text: Repentance is essential to our relationship with God.
options: Transform our heart and restore us
exercises.answer: Transform our heart and restore us
exercises.explanation: True repentance transforms our heart and reconciles us with God.

exercises.statement: God is always ready to forgive those who repent sincerely.
exercises.explanation: God is gracious and always opens His heart to genuine repentance.

exercises.prompt: How should we pray according to God's Word?
exercises.text: Jesus taught us through the Lord's Prayer how to pray correctly.
options: With honesty, faith, and recognition of God
exercises.answer: With honesty, faith, and recognition of God
exercises.explanation: True prayer is genuine communion with God, acknowledging His holiness and grace.

exercises.text: Summary of prayer and repentance
tokens: Create in me a clean heart

exercises.text: There is a time for everything under heaven.
options: There is a time for everything heaven
There is purpose in each season
exercises.answer: There is a time for everything heaven

exercises.text: Journey of spiritual transformation

exercises.statement: Prayer and repentance are essential parts of a healthy life with God.
exercises.explanation: Sincere prayer and genuine repentance keep us connected and transformed by God.
